result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure such as sidewalks and a marked crosswalk, but it is primarily designed for vehicle throughput. The environment is characterized by wide crossing distances, faded pavement markings, and a lack of visible dedicated pedestrian signals.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings in the foreground are significantly worn, reducing visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven asphalt in the roadway and crossing area can create tripping hazards or cause vehicles to swerve.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the intersection and roadway surface

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian walk/don't-walk signals are visible at the signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicle signal timing.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic light poles at the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalks with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and overhead traffic signals in a commercial/industrial setting. While sidewalks are present, the wide roadway and lack of visible pedestrian-specific signals or refuge islands suggest a vehicle-oriented design.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median or refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of visible pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible to indicate when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking/shoulder area to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Install countdown pedestrian signals to provide clear crossing intervals.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and traffic signals but lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads and modern accessibility features like curb extensions. The environment is primarily commercial with wide asphalt surfaces that may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra stripes are significantly worn, reducing visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to interpret vehicle signals.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic light poles on both sides of the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility continental crosswalk across a multi-lane roadway, but lacks a pedestrian refuge island or visible pedestrian signals. The environment is dominated by commercial land use with wide curb cuts for a gas station, increasing potential conflict points between vehicles and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic without a median or refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Wide Curb Cut
hazards.description: The large, undefined entrance to the gas station creates a wide area where turning vehicles may conflict with pedestrians on the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image at the gas station entrance

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb may obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway near the crosswalk

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a vertical buffer and encourage lower vehicle speeds through traffic calming.
